newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan nuclear power plant operating rate at 80.8%.
newsitem.headline: Japan nuclear power plant operating rate at 80.8%.

text.p: The operating rate of Japan's nuclear power plants in the fiscal year which ended on March 31 was 80.8 percent, up slightly from 80.2 percent a year earlier, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday.
Japan's 50 nuclear power reactors, with a combined capacity of 42.55 million kilowatts (kw), provide about 33 percent of the country's electricity needs.
The number of accidents which required a reactor to be manually stopped increased to 11 in 1996/97, up from nine the previous year, MITI said.
There were no radiation leaks or damage to the environment as a result of the 11 incidents, MITI said.
MITI said the operation rate of Japan's nuclear power plants was high compared to most other major countries.
In 1996, operational rates in South Korea reached 87.5 percent, 75.2 percent in the United States and 68.6 percent in Canada, according to MITI calculations.

Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc's Kashiwazaki Kariwa Number 6 nuclear power reactor with a 1.4 million kw capacity, started operations in November, bringing the total number of nuclear power reactors in Japan to 50.
